items.title: France's Bradley Barcola Reaches Agreement To Join Liverpool From PSG - FOX Sports
items.summary: # France's Bradley Barcola Reaches Agreement To Join Liverpool From PSG. Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola has reportedly reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool following discussions with new manager Andoni Iraola. While the 23-year-old is eager to move to Anfield, the two clubs remain far apart in their valuation of the player. According to L'Équipe, Barcola has reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool. The 23-year-old has informed the French champions that he does not intend to extend his current contract, which is set to expire in the summer of 2028. The same report claims that the France international recently held positive discussions with new Reds manager Iraola and several club executives to outline a potential move to Anfield. ## PSG Demand Massive Transfer Fee. While Barcola has agreed to the move in principle, completing the transfer remains a highly complex operation. However, Barcola's clear preference for a move to Anfield provides the Premier League side with a distinct advantage during these high-stakes discussions.

items.summary: * American ownership of Premier League clubs has steadily increased over the past several years. * Fenway Sports Group is poised to net a chunky return on investment from selling a minority stake in Liverpool FC. * CNBC explores how soccer has become such an attractive asset class in the eyes of investors stateside. From Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney's fairy tale acquisition of a fifth-tier Welsh team captured by the "Welcome to Wrexham" TV series in 2020, to Snoop Dogg's investment in second-division side Swansea City this year, the appetite for collaborations with U.S. pop culture figures is only growing. Almost 16 years later, the Boston-based group is poised to net an enormous return on investment after FSG confirmed it is in talks with a syndicate of investors, led by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia, to offload a significant minority stake in the club.

items.title: رودري نجم منتخب إسبانيا يصل مدريد لإجراء جراحة في الظهر - AOL.com
items.summary: # رودري نجم منتخب إسبانيا يصل مدريد لإجراء جراحة في الظهر. مدريد 27 يوليو/تموز (د ب أ) - وصل رودري نجم مانشستر سيتي الإنجليزي وقائد منتخب إسبانيا الفائز بلقب كأس العالم لكرة القدم إلى العاصمة مدريد لإجراء جراحة في الظهر. ذكرت صحيفة ماركا الإسبانية أن رودري وصل إلى مدريد اليوم الإثنين، وسيخضع لعملية جراحية خلال الساعات القليلة القادمة للتعافي من مشكلة في الظهر. من جانبه، أكد إنزو ماريسكا مدرب مانشستر سيتي في مؤتمر صحفي أن اللاعب سينضم إلى الفريق الإنجليزي بعد إجراء العملية الجراحية. أضاف ماريسكا "رودري سيجري العملية الجراحية يوم الإثنين، وبعدها سيحصل على إجازة للراحة والتعافي قبل العودة إلى الفريق". ويستعد مانشستر سيتي للسفر إلى هونج كونج غدا الثلاثاء بدون عدد من نجومه المشاركين في كأس العالم مثل رودري، والنرويجي إرلينج هالاند والفرنسي ريان شرقي، بالإضافة إلى الوافد الجديد إليوت أندرسون. ويستهدف ريال مدريد ضم رودري لكن النادي الإنجليزي يريد تمديد تعاقد نجمه الإسباني، والذي سينتهي بنهاية الموسم المقبل بناء على رغبة مدرب الفريق.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Producing Series About Football Agent - Telecom Asia Sport
items.summary: # Cristiano Ronaldo Producing Series About Football Agent. **Cristiano Ronaldo, the 41-year-old Portuguese star of Al Nassr, is set to produce a series about a football agent. This news comes from Deadline.**. According to the source, the Portuguese forward is collaborating with director Matthew Vaughn, known for films like 'X-Men: First Class' and the 'Kingsman' series. They are currently working together on a series that explores the daily life of a British football agent. Damian Lewis is expected to play the role of the football agent, with Arsenal legend and France international Thierry Henry also involved in the project. Cristiano Ronaldo will also make an appearance in the series as an actor. The premiere date for the project has yet to be announced. Previously, the star Portuguese forward liked a post accusing FIFA regarding the officiating of Argentina's matches in the 2026 World Cup. items.summary: # Roberto Mancini Appointed Head Coach of Italy National Football Team. **The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) has officially announced the appointment of 61-year-old Roberto Mancini as the new head coach of the national team.**. Mancini takes over from Gennaro Gattuso, who left the role on April 3 after failing to qualify for the 2026 World Cup. From May 2018 to August 2023, Mancini previously managed the Azzurri, leading Italy to victory at the UEFA Euro 2020 and securing two third-place finishes in the UEFA Nations League (2020/2021, 2022/2023). Here are the latest updates regarding the 2026 FIFA World Cup:

1. **FIFA's $20 Billion Plan**: FIFA is planning to create a new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion, which has drawn criticism from UEFA. The funds raised are intended to widen access to soccer and strengthen global participation. [Read more here](https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/fifa-mulls-stake-sale-through-new-20-billion-entity-source-says-2026-07-28/) (Source: Reuters).

2. **Controversy Over FIFA's Plans**: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to create a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors, including the Kushner family, has faced backlash from UEFA, which argues that the governance of football should not be treated as an asset to trade. [Read more here](https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-fifa-investors-kushner-infantino-uefa-8345e0864e3a217632733810c232b423) (Source: AP News).

3. **USMNT's Exit from the World Cup**: The United States men's national team (USMNT) faced a disappointing exit from the World Cup after a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the round of 16. Goalkeeper Matt Freese expressed that he would never get over this loss but emphasized the importance of using the experience to inspire future generations. [Read more here](https://apnews.com/article/usmnt-world-cup-eac2885e67fa5b9c2e0f511f9ae17950) (Source: AP News).

4. **Youth Soccer Accessibility**: Tyler Adams from the USMNT is focusing on improving youth soccer accessibility in the wake of the World Cup, aiming to capitalize on the momentum generated by the tournament. [Read more here](https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/usmnts-tyler-adams-youth-soccer-accessibility-2026-world-cup/) (Source: CBS Sports).

These articles provide insights into the ongoing developments and controversies surrounding the World Cup 2026. If you need more specific information or updates, feel free to ask!

items.summary: ## Browse World. Item 1 of 3 Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Final - Spain v Argentina - New York/New Jersey Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey, U.S. **[1/3]**Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Final - Spain v Argentina - New York/New Jersey Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey, U.S. July 28 (Reuters) - FIFA plans to create a new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion, world soccer's governing body ​said on Tuesday, as it seeks backing from its 211 member associations for the proposal in a move already criticised by UEFA. FIFA is one of the world's wealthiest sporting organisations, generating billions of ​dollars in revenue, largely from broadcasting rights, sponsorship and other commercial deals linked to the World Cup. But it says the money raised can be used to widen access ​to the sport and strengthen global participation, with all net benefits to be reinvested in the game.

items.title: FIFA plan for Kushner-backed $20 billion operation to run World Cup meets fury from Europe's UEFA - AP News
items.summary: President Donald Trump, left, speaks with FIFA President Gianni Infantino as confetti falls at the conclusion of the World Cup championship final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, July 19, 2026. GENEVA (AP) — FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s plan to create a $20 billion company running the World Cup with private investors including the Kushner family was announced Tuesday — and immediately attacked by European soccer body UEFA. “It is not FIFA’s to sell,” UEFA said in a statement. Infantino’s plans to form FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) running competitions like the World Cup and Club World Cup were first reported by The Times of London and the Financial Times. “The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially,” UEFA said Tuesday, responding to the reports of selling stakes in FIFA competitions. “This is about the democratization of football worldwide,” Infantino said in a FIFA statement.

items.title: US goalkeeper Matt Freese says he'll never get over his team's loss to Belgium in the World Cup - AP News
items.summary: ## US goalkeeper Matt Freese says he’ll never get over his team’s loss to Belgium in the World Cup. United States goalkeeper Matt Freese (24) reacts after the World Cup round of 16 soccer match between the United States and Belgium in Seattle, Monday, July 6, 2026. United States goalkeeper Matt Freese (24) reacts after the World Cup round of 16 soccer match between the United States and Belgium in Seattle, Monday, July 6, 2026. (AP) — Goalkeeper Matt Freese admits he’s not quite gotten over the United States’ abrupt exit from the 2026 World Cup following a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the round of 16. “It’s important for us to be aware of the positive outcomes that happened in the tournament as well as use that to inspire new generations to continue to get better — to get past that round of 16, to get past the quarterfinals and make it to the semis and the finals,” Freese said.

Every four years, the World Cup gives us a month of football and a masterclass in how brands, platforms and fans behave when six billion pairs of eyes are watching the same ball. The read is consistent: ‘holidays’ searches are a decent proxy for ‘we just played England.’ Handy to know if you’re in the business of predicting travel demand.

items.title: USMNT's Tyler Adams aims to improve youth soccer accessibility, ride wave of 2026 World Cup - CBS Sports
items.summary: # USMNT's Tyler Adams aims to improve youth soccer accessibility, ride wave of 2026 World Cup. The United States men's national team crashing out of the World Cup in the round of 16 may have been disappointing, but that doesn't mean that it wasn't a memorable experience for both fans and members of the team. From fans outside of hotels to everyone singing "Country Roads" in Seattle, it was a transformative moment for Adams and the USMNT, but it's also one that he wants to make sure can lead to more people playing soccer. It has become a hot-button topic about how the USMNT can improve, and one of the biggest things that can be done is making it simple for people who want to play soccer to do so in a culture where the sport still isn't fully embedded. How U.S. Soccer has to capitalize on the wave of the World Cup to reach new heights.
